slides.slide_title: Introduce soft c /s/ and soft g /dʒ/
slides.teacher_cue: Two related rules today. Soft c: when c comes before e, i, or y it makes /s/ — not /k/. city, face, race, mice, ice. Soft g: when g comes before e, i, or y it makes /dʒ/ — not /g/. page, age, stage, gem, giant. The rule: e, i, y soften both c and g. Before anything else (a, o, u, consonant) they keep their hard sounds: /k/ and /g/.
slides.expected_response: Students apply the soft c and soft g rules to read new words correctly.
slides.correction_move: Establish the rule visually: c before a/o/u = /k/ (cat, cod, cut). c before e/i/y = /s/ (city, face, ice). Same for g: g before a/o/u = /g/ (gap, got). g before e/i/y = /dʒ/ (gem, page). Students sort word cards.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hard /k/ being applied to soft c words and hard /g/ to soft g words.

content_payload.correction_routine: c before i says /s/ in city; c before a stays hard /k/ in cat.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Ask students to choose the word where c is soft and explain the letter that follows c.
slides.expected_response: Students identify city as the soft c word and explain the e-i-y rule.
slides.correction_move: Write both words and underline the vowel after c. Re-state the rule: e, i, y soften c.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students who know the rule verbally but still read city with /k/.

content_payload.correction_routine: g before e says /dʒ/ in gem; g before o stays hard /g/ in go.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Students choose the soft g word and explain why the other word is hard g.
slides.expected_response: Students identify gem as soft g and reject go as hard g.
slides.correction_move: Sort both words under hard g and soft g. Rehearse the e-i-y rule aloud.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students who can do soft c but not soft g.

slides.teacher_cue: Say face — soft c at end, CVCe pattern. Confirm /f/ onset, /eɪ/ vowel, /s/ from soft c. Reveal and blend.

slides.correction_move: Model face orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /p/ on /f/ and /k/ substitution for soft c — it is /s/ here.
